A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIDHALLUC benchmark and DINO-HEAL method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, a human baseline, DINO-HEAL comparisons, and qualitative analyses in Tables 3–13.

after.justification: v2 retains and updates those evaluations and additionally reports QA-verification outcomes and a 300-video GPT-4o distractor-recognition experiment.

M1.justification: DINO-HEAL retains the same attention-head averaging, CLS-token saliency extraction, spatial resizing, sigmoid normalization, and feature reweighting in Section 4, Equations 6–12. No algorithmic or architectural modification is established.

E1.justification: The source datasets, 5,002 videos, and ACH/TSH/STH task coverage remain unchanged. Section 5.1 adds a limited evaluation task: asking GPT-4o to recognize its own generated MCQ distractors on 300 existing videos.

E2.justification: The same ten MLLMs, human baseline, and five DINO-HEAL backbones appear in the corresponding comparisons. Newly cited methods such as COMM and CLIP-DINOiser are discussed but not evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark-preparation protocol gains full-dataset QA verification, with corrections to 939 ACH, 68 TSH, and 38 STH items, affecting evaluation annotations across all categories. Section 3.2 also changes the stated MCQ distractor generator from GPT-4 to GPT-4o. The new distractor-recognition experiment introduces a 300-video testing procedure; these disclosures do not establish that every model was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a QA-quality audit reporting 88.76% accuracy before correction and tests whether GPT-4o recognizes its generated distractors: two correct identifications, 33 incorrect identifications, and 265 abstentions. The existing saliency analysis and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based uncertainty estimates. The newly disclosed deterministic decoding settings concern implementation rather than statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Scores change throughout Tables 3–8. For example, Table 3 changes GPT-4o's TSH accuracy from 83.42% to 82.00% and Gemini-1.5-Pro's from 82.67% to 83.83%, reversing their ranking. Table 4 changes Video-LLaVA's ACH binary scores without/with DINO-HEAL from 23.88/28.89 to 26.84/33.80. These are revised benchmark outcomes, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and DINO-HEAL equations are retained. Supplementary Equations 14–17 repeat the existing scene-transition scoring formulas from Equations 2–5; they introduce no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the largest video-hallucination benchmark covering three hallucination types and introduce training-free DINO-HEAL for mitigation. The headline average improvement of 3.02% and the main contribution statements remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 replaces v1's near-human characterization of GPT-4o with explicit human-performance gaps and removes speculation about proprietary models benefiting from larger datasets or advanced fine-tuning. It also interprets the new distractor-recognition results as suggesting little unfair advantage. The foreground-bias explanation and scene-transition limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies reviewer counts, explains that four human evaluators each answer half the queries with two evaluators per query, and discloses temperature 0, top_k 1, and disabled sampling. These clarify previously reported evaluations without establishing changed decoding settings. The project access URL also changes.

R1.justification: New Supplementary Section A substantially expands positioning against complementary-encoder research, including COMM, CLIP-DINOiser, and Nguyen et al.'s deepfake work. It distinguishes DINO-HEAL's inference-time integration from approaches requiring architectural adjustments or training. Section 2.3 also adds HourVideo and LongVideoBench.

P1.justification: The abstract and numerous paragraphs receive condensation, grammar corrections, and wording refinements while the main section order and narrative remain. The appendix becomes Supplementary Material, with a new opening related-work section shifting the existing sections from A–D to B–E.

P2.justification: The same figure and table collection is retained, with Figure 3 reformatted and Figure 6 moved from PDF page 8 to page 7. Appendix tables and prompt boxes are reflowed; Tables 7 and 8 change from side-by-side placement to vertically stacked placement.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens documented benchmark quality through verification and correction of 1,045 QAs, adds a targeted evaluation-bias check, and clarifies protocols and closely related work. These benefits are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: the introduction retains old DINO-HEAL gains, and Video-LLaVA with DINO-HEAL scores 31.42 on STH in Table 4 but 30.81 in Table 8. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
